summary: Choppiness Index: how much price wandered versus how far it went over 14 bars, from 0 to 100, with bands at 61.8 and 38.2.
overview: The Choppiness Index shows whether the market is trending or moving sideways, in its own pane. High values mean choppy price; low values mean a cleaner trend.
Bands sit at 61.8 and 38.2 by default, and the line takes the trending or choppy color near them.
how: CHOP = 100 x log10(sum of true range over 14 bars / (highest high - lowest low over 14 bars)) / log10(14).
When price travels far in one direction, the range is large relative to the summed true ranges, so CHOP is low.
use: Some traders avoid trend-following ideas while CHOP is above 61.8.
Use readings below 38.2 to see a strong trend in place.
Watch a drop from high readings as a sign a range may be ending.
Pair it with a direction tool, since CHOP shows none.
alerts: Alerts: you can alert on its line crossing a value or the candle close (from the chart's + menu); checked while ZoroCharts is open.
notes: Works on any symbol and timeframe; it only needs candle data.
